latest_user_direction: Develop first F01/F02, preserve actual fighter cockpit and drum volume; use RH elite concept A drum orientation like an airboat and two engines; vary wing mounting and lean hull form.
native_vs_proposed: Native fighter has one axial engine and sideways circular drum. Proposed concepts intentionally reorient fixed drum by 90 degrees and use two engines. Source assets and animations are not edited.

variants.title_ru: Поперечный барабан и крылья в направляющих
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / reference-locked vehicle design.
Create a carefully authored concept for a LIGHT Rheinland pirate FIGHTER, evolving the first F01/F02 ideas with the REORIENTED REAR DRUM and TWO ENGINES from RH elite concept A. This is the user's latest chosen exploration. It must stay compact and fighter-like. Earlier heavy truck-like hulls, huge circular masses and altered cabins were rejected. Use no freighter or demonic design language.

REFERENCES AND PRIORITIES:
IMAGE 1: actual rh_pir_fighter in flight. Mandatory baseline SCALE, cabin placement and slender fighter proportions. It originally has a SIDEWAYS-facing aft disk and one engine; the current proposal intentionally reorients that disk and uses two engines, so those two facts are overridden below.
IMAGE 2: ACTUAL FIGHTER COCKPIT — completely immutable. Preserve the exact native cabin module. It is NOT the elite cabin. The user explicitly objected to previous changed cockpit forms. This reference overrides every other image's cockpit.
IMAGE 3: RH elite concept A. Borrow ONLY the rear circular module's fore-aft-axis ORIENTATION and the pair of compact engines beneath it, as seen in its small SIDE view. Do NOT borrow its cabin, large heavy hull, bigger drum diameter, chunky armour, projections or wing shape.
IMAGE 4: the first fighter concept F01 or F02, which the user preferred. Borrow its restrained Rheinland fighter character, moderate recess/detail density, compact neck and material distribution. Correct its cabin to actual image 2 and preserve source scale image 1. Do NOT copy the former sideways disk orientation.
IMAGE 5: actual fighter baydoor closed/open, for fixed mechanism constraints. Original top rectangular lid slides AFT and a little UP; it is separate from the rear drum.

IMMUTABLE COCKPIT — HIGHEST PRIORITY:
Reuse the exact actual cabin from images 1 and 2, copying its module in each view. Preserve its silhouette, position, height, width, pitch, pane outlines, frame widths and colors. Treat it like a protected supplied photographic insert; do not redesign it to match a stylistic fashion. Tall blunt hanging nose, LARGE sloped blue front windshield, NARROW black/yellow horizontal division and a BROAD CONTINUOUS blue band immediately below it with clipped lower corners; tall side panes with broad original metal framing; small plain original brow, original opaque stepped chin with red side inset and small blue corner slots, separate lower black/yellow bumper band and short tapered polygonal bottom. Not a bubble canopy, small square freight-truck windows, exaggerated convex nose, brown chin box, enlarged jaw or elite low canopy. Do not add armour around/over the cabin. Original fighter cabin module and scale are non-negotiable.
The new hull attaches BEHIND it. The glass and metal framing must look like the source asset even if the new hull is painted more cleanly.

KEY NEW ARCHITECTURE — ORIENTATION CHANGE, NOT GROWTH:
Turn the native rear upright drum 90 DEGREES around the VERTICAL axis so its CYLINDER AXIS RUNS NOSE-TO-TAIL, like the disk of an airboat propulsion unit at the rear. Its ROUND face now looks FORWARD/BACKWARD along the ship; it does NOT face port/starboard.
Critical projection consistency: in TRUE SIDE it is a THIN VERTICAL SLAB/rectangle, NEVER a broad circle. In TOP it is a SHORT WIDE CROSSWISE BAND across the rear, not a long spine. In front-side 3/4 its circular face is visible behind the neck. Exactly one round rear drum.
Keep the original drum DIAMETER AND THICKNESS, or slightly LESS, from image 1. Do not enlarge volume. Complete original cabin height is about 2/3 of the drum diameter; do not inflate the drum to 2-3 cabin heights. Keep the upper crown no higher than native overall height. The turned drum fits well WITHIN original wing span. No new external rings or larger shell.
Airboat analogy means ORIENTATION ONLY. This remains a solid closed industrial sci-fi mechanical drum, not an actual spinning propeller, visible fan blades, skeletal cage or empty ring. A simple recessed circular face with two or three broad grooves/service fields; design details specified below. Drum is FIXED, no proposed new rotation animation.
Exactly TWO compact axial engine pods, paired symmetrically below/alongside the rear drum, axes nose-to-tail and no central third engine. Each pod diameter only about HALF original cabin width. Rear exhausts point aft. Integrated solid short fairings, no exposed support bars. Engines do not fold with wings.
Keep overall compact fighter mass and length comparable to source W10.9 H7.1 L13.6. No enlarged abdomen, tall armour tower, oversized heavy-fighter engines or wide cargo-body silhouette. Source cabin size is the scale anchor.

HULL / STYLE:
Narrow neck, coherent angular wedge planes and a lean lower silhouette. Develop the first F01/F02 approaches through deep CUT-IN side pockets and meaningful shifts of planes, not raised plates or bolt-on armour. Slightly less central-hull visual mass than those first concepts. Piracy through rough fitted repair sections: one diagonal donor seam, mismatched muted red/olive flush inset, repaired side panel with a slightly different outline, restrained scuffs. Enough moderate useful medium detail to model: a few recesses, slide channels, hatch landings, enclosed joints and inset grille. No tiny greeble carpets, decorative rivets, repeated raised ribs, heavy weathering or giant military crosses.
No demons, horns, claws, spikes, skulls, Corsair grammar, exposed pipes/hoses/rods/cables, external frames/trusses/braces, detached hoops or floating parts. Necessary solid hinge housings and engines may protrude modestly, all decorative detail mainly recessed.

WING / CARGO MECHANICS:
Two wing assemblies, each inner sliding carrier plus separate outer hinged panel. Native flight span/area and modest downward droop. Short broad angular wings sweep FORWARD: TOP nose UP, outer tips are UP-LEFT / UP-RIGHT from roots; SIDE nose RIGHT, wing extends down-RIGHT. No backward swept jet, flat delta or huge knife wings. Original stowing moves carriers IN/UP/AFT, outer tips roll UP ~63 degrees on fore-aft hinge axes. Leave clear articulation and sweep, no fixed bridge over a moving joint. Keep engines stationary; wings have separate sockets.
Baydoor is the original rectangular lid immediately behind the cabin; show CLOSED. It must slide AFT and slightly UP. Keep its central travel corridor and an unobstructed receiving pocket UNDER the turned drum's elevated base, between the two engine housings. No solid fan base or crossbar blocking that path. Do not turn the round drum into a cargo door, do not change to a rotating hatch. Keep cargo-bay walls and floor.

PAGE:
One landscape sheet, THREE coherent views of the SAME design: dominant front-side 3/4 LEFT, exact SIDE / FLIGHT upper RIGHT nose RIGHT, TOP / FLIGHT lower RIGHT nose UP. Full silhouettes, no extra inset. The rear circle must be thin edge-on in SIDE and short-wide edge-on in TOP; this is essential to the concept. Two rear engine pods visible in TOP and perspective. All views show flight configuration and the same original cabin.
Clean technical concept rendering with crisp surface boundaries and quiet shaded material fields, less painterly and less noisy than F01/F02; original cabin copied faithfully. Neutral light warm-gray background, worn gray/olive metal with restrained faded red panels. No scene or effects. Title specified below, plus view labels only. Do not add arrows likely to misrepresent motion.

F03 — RECESSED WING CARRIAGES:
Develop F01's narrow angular neck into a lower, tapered wedge with a rising underside toward the original cabin. One long trapezoidal recessed side service field and a short deep three-vane grille, with a diagonal repaired red insert. Wing inner sliding carriers sit in clearly visible recessed oblique rectangular channels BELOW the mid-neck and AHEAD of the engines. Give each carrier a short nested solid sleeve; at the inner/outer boundary a modest fore-aft cylindrical hinge is half buried into a clean polygonal bearing housing. The two wing joints are structurally readable without giant external pods. Wings are thin, forward-swept, broad with clipped tips, one slightly different flush repaired outer section.
The REORIENTED rear drum has a restrained native-sized circular rim and a deeply inset closed circular face. Three broad parallel horizontal recesses cross only its central face, with solid back walls; one small asymmetrical red repair field on the lower face. NO turbine blades or decorative spokes. The shell curves are continuous, no enlarged halo. Paired small engines are close underneath the left/right lower quadrants; compact and tucked into the aft body, leaving the center lid-receiving channel free. No oversized upper shoulders.
Title exactly: RH PIRATE FIGHTER / F03

Three broad inset slats and a small off-center service hatch, closed solid floor. No new outer armour, no bigger diameter, no projecting hub. Two small separate engines tucked against the drum's lower flanks, a little wider apart than F03 but still inside native wing span and no larger.
